name: Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic
definition: The largest absolute difference between the empirical cumulative distribution functions of two samples, taken over every value either sample holds. It lies between 0 and 1, is 0 for samples with the same values, is 1 for samples that don't overlap, and counts tied values once in each sample's function.
citations: W. J. Conover, Practical Nonparametric Statistics, 3rd edition, Wiley, 1999, section 6.3 (the Smirnov test).
Myles Hollander, Douglas A. Wolfe, and Eric Chicken, Nonparametric Statistical Methods, 3rd edition, Wiley, 2014, chapter 5.

properties.says: [1, 1, 2] against [1, 2, 2] gives 1/3: ties step both functions at once.
Swapping the samples doesn't change the statistic.

provenance.why: Issue #9653 names it in the starting list of distance primitives and two-sample statistics. The issue was written after reading one task's winning runs, so that task counts as a source.
